findings.statement: verifying block checksums costs nothing on a cold scan
findings.detail: cold scans at 66531652 entries/s verified against 81801331 unverified (verified vs unverified: less 0.813x (p=0.0122, rel_iqr 1.7%/10.3%)). f8-checksums measured this cost at no difference on point reads, where a block is checked once and read many times; a scan over a fresh reader touches each block for the first time and pays for all of them

findings.statement: a scan's first pass costs no more than its steady state
findings.detail: verified: 66531652 entries/s cold against 87547276 warm (1.32x). Unverified: 81801331 against 80755418 (0.99x). Whatever remains after the checksum is subtracted is the cost of touching the mapping for the first time, and the cold pass took 0 major faults with 0.0% of its wall time off CPU

notes: one file with checksums in it; the arms differ only in whether the reader verifies them. A fresh reader per repetition is what makes the first pass cold
